notes: Shotgun (short interference-tube) RF condenser microphone, not rack-mountable (handheld/mounted mic body, so rackUnits omitted). Single 3-pin XLR (XLR3M on the mic body) serves as both the balanced audio output and the phantom-power input (P48, 48V ±4V, ~2mA draw) — there is no separate power connector. No grade applies since XLR3/analog audio is not in the bandwidth-graded connector families. Confirmed via Sennheiser's official product page (sennheiser.com/en-us/catalog/products/microphones/mkh-416-p48u3/mkh-416-p48u3-001511), which is the authoritative source used here. The official product-spec PDF (assets.sennheiser.com) returned HTTP 403 and could not be fetched directly, and B&H's page also returned 403, but the manufacturer's own catalog page provided complete, consistent connector/power data corroborated by multiple secondary search snippets (manual excerpts, retailer listings) all citing "3-pin XLR" and "48V phantom power (P48)".

ports.name: Audio Output
ports.note: 3-pin XLR balanced output; also receives P48 (48V ±4V) phantom power from the connected preamp/recorder to power the RF condenser capsule (~2 mA draw). No separate power connector on the microphone.
